![A Genos task's activity: the comment Claude wrote carries Claude's mark, the user's own changes do not](/lp/shots/en/record.webp)

You asked Claude to file the follow-ups from this afternoon and to note where a task stands. It said it was done. A few days later a teammate asks about one of those comments: "Did you write this?"

## Why it is hard

Once an AI can write into your team's workspace, its words and yours can look the same. They are posted under your name, because it works as you.

Then you are left guessing. Was this status something you checked, or something the AI concluded? Is this note your decision, or its summary of one? You either trust all of it or reread all of it, and your teammates have the same problem with none of your context.

## How Genos helps

Connect an AI app such as Claude and its writes are marked: in task history, on comments and in note history. Claude on claude.ai and Claude Desktop shows Claude's own mark; other apps, Claude Code included, show a connected-app mark. What you type in Genos has none.

```flow
Your AI writes
Genos marks it
You check the marked lines
Fix or delete
```

So the question "did you write this?" has an answer on the screen. Open the task's **Activity** tab and you can read down it: this comment came from the connected app, this priority change was you.

## What you get

- **A quick review.** After a session with your AI, look for the marks instead of rereading the whole task.
- **Honest hand-offs.** A teammate can see which lines an AI wrote and weigh them accordingly.
- **A way to correct it.** The comments and notes are yours: edit or delete them. Note version history and the task's description history let you go back to an earlier text.
- **Limits you set first.** The app only sees what you can see in the teams you chose, and deleting stays off unless you allow it.

Know one thing before you start: a connected app writes at once, within the access you gave it. It does not stop to ask inside Genos. The mark is how you see afterwards what it did, and by default Genos also alerts you about riskier actions such as deletes or sharing changes.

## How to start

1. Open **Settings → Developer** and connect your AI (Core and above).
2. Work with it as usual. Genos asks the connected app to record tasks, decisions and progress.
3. Open a task it touched and read its **Activity** tab.
